project_dependencies.use: Frozen PG37 commentary, affix identities and inherited lexical lists.
PG37 owns the paired rule and the root-only inheritance.
PG769 owns the adjoining verse, Bhaṭṭi 4.17.
PG14 full carrier, history pairing and specialization.

source_observations.observation: Pairs the lists, senses and suffixes in order. The fruit examples retain k and the ear example retains j.
Specifies that the initial k and j are pronounced. Retain final markers under their own suffix histories.
The joined consonant spelling and the list containing both mukha and makha are local textual facts.
Only the root member of the preceding coordinated senses carries forward. Its example identifies the first lunar day.
Distinguishes transformation and beginning. Discusses selective inheritance despite the common prescription.
The female figure bears the ear-root adjective. The moon comparison contains the temporal locative.

source_observations.locator: Jayamaṅgalā on Bhaṭṭi 4.16, stanza serial 154, printed p. 76
source_observations.observation: Inside her adjective the eyes reach the two ear roots. The omitted participle and the internal dual belong to the prose analysis. The lunar day is explicitly identified.

source_observations.locator: Amarakośa with Sudhā, Siṃhādivarga, digital page 207
source_observations.observation: Names the wing root among bird terms and marks pakṣati as feminine.
Opens the sequence with Agni, Sarasvatī and Soma.
The first rib is situated at the root of the right side. The next rib is nipakṣati.

source_observations.locator: Mādhyandina Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā 25.4, Saṃhitā and Pada
source_observations.observation: The Pada distinguishes pakṣatiḥ and ni-pakṣatiḥ. The first three deity allocations are Agni, Vāyu and Indra.
Optional nadī designation before ṅ-marked singular obliques of short feminine i. The worked example is mati.

source_observations.locator: MDU Sanskrit Vyākaraṇa, ikārānta feminine mati
source_observations.observation: Independent case model including instrumental yā, dual bhyām and plural bhiḥ. Supplies inflectional evidence for the written application.
